行政長官李家超今到立法會參與首場「對談交流會」，會後與立法會主席李慧琼會見傳媒。李家超回應宏福苑長遠居住安排時，指已有 53％ 業主簽訂買賣協議，籲住戶「把握時間作決定」。 他另回應陳嘉信涉司法抄襲被提早退休事件，指尊重首席法官採適當措施，維護公眾對法官獨立專業履責的信心。至於黃錦輝涉醉駕請辭而空缺的議席，會否進行補選，李家超指未來 18 個月有三場重要選舉，認為在時間、工作、相對必要性方面，應先做好這三場選舉。

Chief Executive John Lee today attended the first "dialogue and exchange session" at the Legislative Council and responded to media questions afterwards.

53% of owners have signed purchase agreements; nearly 91% have signed letters accepting the acquisition offer

When asked about the progress of the Wang Fuk Court acquisition and whether the reasons of residents who had not yet signed the consent forms had been explored, Lee said the matter had been handled with "empathy, reason and the law" all along. He reiterated that regarding the long-term accommodation arrangements, the government was acquiring the property titles at a price of HK$8,000 to HK$10,500 per square foot, and was also bearing various risks, including the uncertainty of insurance compensation and the possibility of different legal proceedings.

He said that as of yesterday, 90.8% of owners had signed letters accepting the acquisition proposal and 53% had completed signing the sale and purchase agreements, with some owners having formally completed the title transfers. He described the process as smooth and said, "I hope everyone will seize the time to make a decision." He also said the decision was of course for each household to make after weighing their actual circumstances, but as for the acquisition price, the risks borne, and other assistance provided, "the hope is to enable the relevant households to make a decision as soon as possible, so that everyone can return to normal life at an early date." He also said some units would soon be put up for residents' consideration, and "this is an opportunity everyone should seize early — it may be possible to apply for a long-term residence of your choice."

Lee also reiterated that the government had recently optimised the rental subsidy arrangements, and that the HK$1 billion funding application to the Legislative Council for the acquisition of Wang Chi Court had also been approved. He said the government would continue with its explanatory work, and that households with questions or requests could relay them to the dedicated outreach teams or the one-household-one-social-worker scheme, which would handle matters flexibly and pragmatically according to actual circumstances.

Asked about the long-term housing arrangements for Wang Fuk Court, Lee said 53% of owners had signed purchase agreements, with some having completed title transfers, and described the process as smooth.

Response on Chan Ka-shun's plagiarism and early retirement: respect for the Chief Justice's appropriate measures

As for the Court of First Instance judge Chan Ka-shun being exposed for multiple instances of plagiarism and being required by Chief Judge Andrew Cheung yesterday to take early retirement, when asked whether this was sufficient to restore public confidence, Lee said the community had high expectations of judges and professional standards, and the judiciary had always operated and managed its affairs independently. He said he respected the Chief Justice's adoption of appropriate measures to maintain public confidence in the independent and professional fulfilment of judicial duties by judges, and he was confident that judges and judicial officers at all levels would abide by the judicial oath and fulfil their judicial responsibilities with diligence, independence and professionalism.

High Court judge Chan Ka-shun, involved in judicial plagiarism, has been required to take early retirement. The Chief Executive responded today saying he respects the Chief Justice's adoption of appropriate measures to maintain public confidence. (File photo)

Separately, the University of Hong Kong (HKU) President Zhang Xiang, who was previously embroiled in campus governance controversy, said yesterday that he would step down after completing two terms totalling 10 years in 2028. When asked for his assessment and whether he would require HKU to include clauses in the appointment of a new president to maintain good communication with the Council, Lee said Zhang was a scientist passionate about science who longed to return to the laboratory to solve scientific problems and contribute to society. He thanked Zhang for giving advance notice of his decision to the Council, allowing the university sufficient time to recruit a new president.

Lee also thanked Zhang for his hard work and contributions to HKU during his past and future tenure as president. He said the appointment of the president would be handled by the Council, noting that the universities had well-functioning mechanisms for recruiting presidents. He expressed confidence in the Council's handling of the matter and believed it could ensure the new president would lead HKU in sustained development and continuous progress.

HKU President Zhang Xiang announced yesterday that he would step down in 2028. Lee said he was grateful for his contributions to HKU and expressed confidence that the Council would handle the recruitment work well. (File photo)

Wong Kam-fai's resignation: no by-election for now — priority is to hold the upcoming three elections well

Legislative Council member Wong Kam-fai was arrested for drink-driving late last month and resigned earlier this month. There is public concern about whether a by-election will be held. Secretary for Constitutional and Mainland Affairs Clementina Cheng had earlier indicated that time was tight. When asked again today about the by-election, Lee said three important elections would be held in the next 18 months: the Election Committee election this November, the Chief Executive election next March, and the District Council election before the end of next year. He said for any election, the Electoral Affairs Commission (EAC) would consider a combination of factors, including human resources, venue arrangements, polling station setup, and the procurement and transportation of election materials. It would need to consider the overall work arrangements and the relative necessity of each election based on actual circumstances.

Lee continued that after the Election Committee election is completed in November this year, it will take office on 1 February next year to perform its role in the relevant elections. He believed that compared with a by-election for one vacancy in the Legislative Council, "in terms of time, workload and relative necessity, priority should be given to holding these three elections well."

Following Wong Kam-fai's resignation over a drink-driving charge, attention from various sectors has focused on whether a by-election will be held for the vacant seat. Lee said priority should be given to the upcoming three elections, while Legislative Council President Starry Lee said she respected the assessments of the Chief Executive and the EAC.

When asked whether the reduction in the number of members would affect the work of the Legislative Council, and whether she had spoken with Xia Baolong, Starry Lee said she understood and respected the assessments of the Chief Executive and the EAC. She noted that as an important working partner of the government, the Legislative Council would certainly first cooperate with and support the delivery of a series of important tasks, including the first Five-Year Plan and the Policy Address. She continued that although there had been changes in the Legislative Council, with only 89 members remaining, "I believe every member understands the need to go the extra mile, to support and share the burden with each other, because of new circumstances arising from unpredictable changes." She said all members would give their all, and with the joint efforts of the 89 members, the full functions of the Council would continue to be delivered as in the past.
